structured_output.hypothesis: In a global naturalised-flora checklist, far more European-native plant species are naturalised in the La Plata region (Argentina/Uruguay) and Australia than southern-hemisphere-native species are naturalised in Europe, and the La Plata excess is at least as large as Australia's.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Let N_S be the number of European-native vascular plant species naturalised in Argentina plus Uruguay (and, separately, in Australia). Let N_N be the number of species with an exclusively southern-hemisphere native range that are naturalised in any European GloNAF region. The claim passes if all three hold. (1) N_S / N_N >= 10 for La Plata and also for Australia. (2) Southern-hemisphere-native species make up <= 5% of Europe's naturalised flora. (3) The European-origin share of the naturalised flora is larger in Argentina/Uruguay than in Australia.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim fails if either N_S / N_N < 3 for La Plata or for Australia, or if southern-hemisphere-native species make up > 15% of Europe's naturalised flora. A ratio between 3 and 10, or a share between 5% and 15%, is inconclusive and counts as not confirmed. Condition (3) failing on its own counts as a partial failure of the 'lesser degree' clause.
structured_output.interpretation: 'European productions' and 'southern forms' are read as vascular plant species, because Darwin's examples are mainly plants and GloNAF is plant-only. 'Naturalised' is read as GloNAF's status of established, self-sustaining alien populations. 'La Plata' is read as the GloNAF regions of Argentina (especially the Pampas/Buenos Aires provinces) and Uruguay. 'Australia' is read as the Australian states and territories. 'Any part of Europe' is read as GloNAF's European regions. 'Southern forms' is read as taxa whose native range lies wholly in the southern hemisphere (South America, southern Africa, Australasia). Native ranges are not given in GloNAF itself, so they must be joined from an external source such as the TDWG-based Plants of the World Online or WCVP native distributions. 'Partly displaced the natives' cannot be measured in a checklist and is not tested. Only the asymmetry in naturalisation counts is tested. This is a modern reinterpretation of Darwin's qualitative statement as species counts, with the caveat that checklist sampling effort differs among regions.

dataset.name: Global Naturalized Alien Flora (GloNAF) database
dataset.why_it_fits: GloNAF lists naturalised vascular plant taxa by region worldwide, including Argentina, Uruguay, Australian states and European countries and regions. The fields used would be region/country, taxon name and naturalisation status. Each taxon's native range would be joined from an external standard source (POWO/WCVP) to classify it as European-native or southern-hemisphere-native. Counts of the two directions of exchange are then compared. I did not verify the current download and DOI details, so the DOI is left null rather than guessed.
